strings.100_village_swamp_after_1: The fairy says I already have all the power I need... As long as I use my own faith.
strings.100_village_swamp_after_3: I'll find my own way back!
strings.100_village_swamp_bandits_1: Hey... you can pass, but him...
strings.100_village_swamp_bandits_2: Ha ha! The Old Goddess will punish you!
strings.100_village_swamp_bandits_3: For everything you've done to her sacred land!
strings.100_village_swamp_bandits_4: Sven, this guy is insane... just let him through.
strings.100_village_swamp_faith_2: It took me some time to gather all of this.
strings.100_village_swamp_faith_3: Oh, don't be modest. I know you produce faith on an industrial scale.
strings.100_village_swamp_faith_4: A true priest of the Ancient God...
strings.100_village_swamp_faith_6: Yes... lead me to the shrine!
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_10: Once, the world was in balance.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_11: But greed turned them against you.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_12: In their greed they began to hate you.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_13: You were betrayed... and left alone...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_14: Yet I am here to worship you.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_16: I hear you... and I feel all your faith...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_18: I have so many questions... I need your power...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_19: Excuse me... I have a rather delicate matter...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_21: I just checked my notes... I think I still owe you some coins for your teeth.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_23: Follow me... let the Goddess speak with the Keeper.
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_3: Worshipers sure aren't what they used to be...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_4: If you don't like me, I can leave!
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_6: Alright... I'm ready. Tell me when to start...
strings.100_village_swamp_goddess_8: Alright... wish me luck. This is my first time...
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_2: Maybe if I knew something about him, it would help me find him.
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_3: He used to be a good boy... always playing those G&G games...
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_4: He lived in fantasy worlds... always inventing new ones.
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_5: Then we were in a car... and then suddenly, we appeared here...
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_6: The portal made us gods, and my brother finally got to create his own little Roman Empire.
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_7: That was many, many years ago...
strings.100_village_swamp_optional_8: These memories so tire me... Go. Find him.
strings.100_village_swamp_outpost_1: Hey folks, do you know where I'm going?
strings.100_village_swamp_outpost_3: I'm going to awaken the Goddess of Nature.
strings.100_village_swamp_outpost_4: Good thing we elected Heffry instead of that guy.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_1: The Man with the Red Eye.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_10: That's all there is. There's no magical yellow arrow, my friend.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_11: One other detail... the place smells terrible.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_12: Probably the sewers. I should talk to the Looter at the Port Club.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_13: Maybe they can give me a hint.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_14: Just think... perhaps my brother has already sent you some clues.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_2: Do you have enough power to find your brother?
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_3: Mmm... I haven't felt this good in years!
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_5: Oh... he's very weak. Nearly powerless.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_7: Buildings, streets, zombies... all right above him. Rivers surround it on three sides.
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_8: It's like a cell, but not meant for humans...
strings.100_village_swamp_red_eye_9: Hm... I was hoping for something more specific...
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_1: I need some rest... and a snack.
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_2: Alright, let's just get this over with.
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_3: I brought some of your cheese.
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_5: Weird... two wheels of cheese appeared under my bed.
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_6: Right after we talked about the ritual.
strings.100_village_swamp_rest_7: I figured it was a gift from you.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_11: There's nobody anymore who wants to work in a good old manufactory.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_12: This might surprise you, but... I have plenty of workers willing to work at my factory.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_13: At least, I hope they're willing... It's better than what they'd be doing otherwise.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_14: Your factory? With conveyor belts and automated workbenches?
strings.101_workshop_calculations_16: Oh, I'd love to see that!
strings.101_workshop_calculations_17: Now that you're so excited, I feel like I should meet certain expectations...
strings.101_workshop_calculations_18: As soon as I check everything over, I'll gladly invite you for a tour.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_2: So, what's this calculation were you talking about?
strings.101_workshop_calculations_22: We'll never achieve the finest quality steel from the Royal Foundry.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_24: We might not need to.. Some days ago, I saw smoke coming out of it.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_25: We just need someone to reach it, and check whether the iron masters are still producing steel.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_26_a: Lucky for you... I'm already working on that.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_26_b_1: Is it far? How do we get there?
strings.101_workshop_calculations_26_b_2: It's on the north side of the town.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_26_b_3: The only way to reach it is through a water tunnel.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_26_b_4: Luckily, I know all about it.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_27: I'll bring you some samples, and you can check the quality.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_29: Just great... meanwhile, I still have 25 years of work ahead of me...
strings.101_workshop_calculations_4: See these numbers... even with all the resources I have, it'll take 25 years to reach pre-apocalypse levels.
strings.101_workshop_calculations_5: And that was only supposed to be the beginning...
strings.101_workshop_calculations_6: I see... so what's the problem, now that your resources are covered?
strings.101_workshop_calculations_8: I'm all alone here... Even if I built a factory, there'd be no one to work in it...
strings.101_workshop_calculations_9: They barely escaped death, but they're all too refined for hard work.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_11: That was a great story! You said you had more?
strings.102_town_captain_beer_12: Yeah... but now I’m sad... and not in the mood for another one.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_13: All my stories are in the past... and as for what's awaiting me... well, I already have gray hair.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_14: Maybe another beer will cheer you up.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_15: Nah... I'll need something stronger than beer... if I'm gonna believe I still have any decent stories ahead.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_2: Ah, good... you know, I’ve seen you before.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_4: I thought we’d end up on some grand adventure together... but no.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_5: Then I saw you again... It felt like a sign. Have you any adventures to share?
strings.102_town_captain_beer_6: Honestly, I can’t think of any right now.
strings.102_town_captain_beer_7: I see... you know, I consider myself quite a remarkable character...
strings.102_town_captain_faith_2: Trust me... you have adventures still ahead of you. Just give it time.
strings.102_town_captain_faith_3: ... You know what? I believe you. Want to hear another story?
strings.102_town_captain_faith_4: Heh... telling these stories just makes me sad...
strings.102_town_captain_meet_1: Hey... want to hear one of my stories?
strings.102_town_captain_meet_3: Only the best. I used to be a captain... until my ship sank.
strings.102_town_captain_meet_4: Buy me a beer and I’ll prove it.
strings.103_workshop_steel_10: But there aren't any masters left there.
strings.103_workshop_steel_12: A group of monks live there now. They run the foundry.
strings.103_workshop_steel_13: Monks... mastering steel and producing this?
strings.103_workshop_steel_15: But that's unbelievable! How could they? It would take years...
strings.103_workshop_steel_16: By the way, I cleared the way to the foundry. We can trade with them now.
strings.103_workshop_steel_17: Good news... but still — how did they do it? Even I couldn't master the process.
strings.103_workshop_steel_18: No idea. They just work together. Calmly.
strings.103_workshop_steel_2: Jack, I brought an ingot from the Royal Foundry.
strings.103_workshop_steel_3: See if it's still any good.
strings.103_workshop_steel_5: There's a simple test for that.
strings.103_workshop_steel_8: No... quite the opposite. It's better than ever.
strings.103_workshop_steel_9: It looks like the iron masters finally perfected their craft.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_11: And no toilet breaks either, I bet...
strings.104_workshop_industrial_12: Did you really build all of this?
strings.104_workshop_industrial_13: Mostly. The space and the underfloor belt gears were already here.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_14: I just repaired and connected them.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_15: And this is under the Inquisitor's base, right?
strings.104_workshop_industrial_18: The king used this place to produce goods for the entire town.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_19: It was so cheap, the guilds could barely compete.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_2: I have something I think might impress you.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_20: He had a perfect monopoly. Prisoners probably did all the work.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_21: Well... I'm glad everything is in good hands now.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_22: It's incredible you achieved all this so quickly...
strings.104_workshop_industrial_23: You're meeting the entire town's demands...
strings.104_workshop_industrial_24: You've surpassed everything I ever imagined.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_25: Let's go back... to my... humble shack...
strings.104_workshop_industrial_4: Exactly. I think I'm ready to show it.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_5: This is my modern production line.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_6: Unbelievable... it's bigger than anything I've ever seen.
strings.104_workshop_industrial_7: Conveyor belts everywhere... but where does all the power come from?
strings.104_workshop_industrial_8: You see those guys running, turning the wheels?
strings.105_guards_armor_10: I'll keep them safe. If things go bad again, they'll earn the right to wear them.
strings.105_guards_armor_12: Life taught me to be. I never had things easy, so I learned to prepare for the worst.
strings.105_guards_armor_13: I'm tired, Keeper... and not the kind of tired that a good sleep can fix.
strings.105_guards_armor_14: I think you've done enough. You've earned a peaceful life.
strings.105_guards_armor_15: Yeah... I think I am ready to retire. Now it's your problem... Ha ha.
strings.105_guards_armor_16_a_1: Agatha offered me a corner in her place. My first real home in my life... I've always lived in the barracks.
strings.105_guards_armor_16_a_2: Strange how a crossroads can become so peaceful.
strings.105_guards_armor_16_b_1: I'll find myself a little place nearby. I'd like to live closer to Agatha.
strings.105_guards_armor_18: Good thing I pack light. My sword, my memories... my new armor... and that's about it.
strings.105_guards_armor_2: This armor is a true masterpiece... exactly what you asked for.
strings.105_guards_armor_3: Ha... Every master brags about his creations...
strings.105_guards_armor_4: But this one really deserves it. It's incredible. Better than the King's Guard used to wear.
strings.105_guards_armor_5: One for you. The rest for your lads.
strings.105_guards_armor_6: Mine goes on display. The others I'll keep oiled and carefully stored.
strings.105_guards_armor_7: I thought you were going to give them to your guards.
strings.105_guards_armor_8: Oh, they're safe for now... all thanks to you.
strings.105_guards_armor_9: Those lazy fools would just scratch them on the tavern benches, or pawn them for ale.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_1: Let us pray for good steel, brothers!
strings.106_foundry_meeting_10: You're eight years older now... and your eyes give you away.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_12: Yours challenge the world. His only endured it.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_13: I see you know a lot. And that's good.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_14: I have expected this day. I've prepared my answers.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_16: Can you tell me about the other version of me?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_17: Was he a villain who destroyed the world?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_18: He was... and still is... my friend.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_19: He wanted to fix things. It all just ended in the usual way.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_20: So... was the zombie apocalypse his fault?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_21: I hope not... Honestly I don't know how it could be done without portal magic.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_22: We removed it from the palace — the portal and all its magic.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_24: We all began abusing it for our own benefit.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_25: But in our defense, it was the Keeper's wife who started it.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_26: She always wanted more. Power. A crown. Nonsense.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_27: So six of us activated the portal, and stole it away from the Royal Palace.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_29: I only hope it wasn't because of us.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_4: I told you not to call me that... please.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_5: Dear me... and who is this? A new Graveyard Keeper.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_6: Familiar, yet entirely different. Ha ha...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_7: Please continue the service without me, brothers.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_8: How did you realize I'm not the same Keeper?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_11: Hm... what should I ask for... I don't actually need anything personally...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_12: Then maybe you can just give me the portal piece?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_13: No, no... ha ha... that's not how things work here. Let's see...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_14: My brothers are tired of pumping the bellows by hand.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_15: I can send you some zombies...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_16: Oh, we don't need whole zombies here...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_17: Alright, I’ll bring you just zombie power.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_18: I'm not sure, but it might work.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_19: Ha ha... I haven't given anyone a quest in eight years...
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_3: As you wish. It's quite simple.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_4: Mirror... mirror... show me the first part of the magic portal.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_5: You are the most beautiful, of course... wait... what? The portal part... give me a second.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_6: Very funny... it's right behind you!
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_8: So I can take the first piece and use the mirror to find the others?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_mirror_9: Of course. But first, you'll need to do my quests.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_11: Yes. Your other self brought her here. That was a mistake.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_12: The mirror can reveal the location of the next portal fragment.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_13: The magic is a little fancy, so for the first time... we'll use it together.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_2: I need to find the magic portal and use it to save the world.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_3: My brother and I stole it from the Palace... from your other self.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_4: Your wife wished to become a queen, moved into the Palace, and took the portal with her.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_5: We split it up, so they couldn't recover it and use it again.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_6: Interesting... and where are the pieces now?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_7: That's a very good question. I scattered seven pieces among different people.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_portal_9: Fortunately, I took a magic mirror from your wife.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_10: Vagner? Hmm... you mean the astrologer, Gunter?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_11: Call him whatever you like. I think you know who I mean.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_12: That mirror is kind of rude.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_3: You know what? You seem like a decent fellow.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_5: Thank you, I guess... So can I have the mirror?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_6: Sure... but could you try it here to find the next piece... just to make sure it works.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_8: Mirror... mirror... show me the second portal fragment.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_quest_9: The second piece lies in the home of your friend... the poet, Vagner.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_10: Ha ha... not quite. We've also studied every metallurgy book we could find.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_11: I see. So can I get some of that steel?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_12: Of course. Ha ha. It is for sale.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_2: Hey, I see the smelting furnace is still working.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_3: Indeed it is. First it boiled the water for our baths, and now it smelts the finest steel.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_4: So you're still making high-quality steel?
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_6: But how? And why? You're monks... you're supposed to make wine at the very most.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_7: It's part of our vow of obedience.
strings.106_foundry_meeting_steel_8: We gather around the furnace and pray to its spirit.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_10: I could command all the attention I once craved... but I didn't need it then.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_11: I think you're trying to say that friendship is more important than public approval.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_12: Well said... And now it's time to help my friend Jack.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_14: Patience. Jack has to approve it first.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_15: Plus, a project of this scale deserves a proper announcement.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_a_1: About Jack... I believe he'll agree to join you.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_a_2: That's great. I'll talk to him. We'll make this project right here at the port!
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_b_1: Heh... I think Jack is still refusing to let go of his factory.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_b_2: But I'll show him I can handle the Town's production needs myself.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_b_3: Sure... just be gentle with him. He tries to look tougher than he is.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_16_b_4: In the meantime, I'll get everything ready. We'll launch the project at the port.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_3: Excellent. I knew we were on the correct trajectory.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_5: Poet. Magical Beast. Astrologer. And now — PR strategist.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_6: You perfected the Magic Beast role?
strings.107_astrologer_likes_7: Yeeeh... it was a brief, but very dramatic part of my life.
strings.107_astrologer_likes_8: I might have liked that role the most... I was part of something big. Just like now.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_10: I don't know what they wished for last time... but now the day of the week are a total mess.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_11: And apparently, I'm the only one who notices... the Astrologer.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_12: Ok, maybe the days will get back to normal after we fix the world.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_13: Fine... Perhaps fixing time itself is part of saving the world.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_14: Mirror... mirror... reveal the third portal fragment.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_15: Interesting... Would you care to explain, or shall I?
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_16: You want to tell him yourself?
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_17: You see... I once had two fragments. Charm gave me hers.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_18: But I wasn't always a respected PR manager and astrologer.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_19: Back then, I needed the money... so I sold it.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_2: I know you have the second pice of the portal. Mirrors don't lie.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_21: In my defense, I got an excellent price... even for a magical relic.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_23: Somewhere in the middle of the sea.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_24: It left on a merchant ship.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_26: Relax. We can buy it back. Everything is negotiable. Speak to the Trade Master at the Main Pier.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_28: After all, what kind of story would this be if the hero couldn't fix his mistakes?
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_3: Ah, so you visited Brother Bishop... he used to be quite the man of fashion, you know.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_30: You have a point. Now go and talk with the Trade Master.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_5: So, Gunter... or should I say Vagner — where's the fragment?
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_6: It's here. I always hoped someone would come and restore the portal.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_7: If the Bishop trusted you with the mirror, I suppose I can trust you too.
strings.108_astrologer_pieces_8: I just hope you'll ask about fixing the days of the week.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_10: Yes. Kind. To people. Ridiculous of course.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_11: It's actually a good thing to be kind to others.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_12: Oh, how fortunate for me... so, Mr. Kindness. I think I'll ask you for some help.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_13: I'm ready. Especially if it proves I'm right.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_14: It's... delicate. I need to choose my words carefully.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_2: I did what I could. The church looks magnificent.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_3: For once... I don't feel like shouting at you.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_4: Those readings are bringing out my soft side...
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_5: And I might even enjoy it.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_6: That's not a bad thing, you know.
strings.109_crossroad_magnificent_8: He says I should be... what was it... ki... kin...
strings.10_village_food_samples_2: This is the best harvest we've had in some time.
strings.10_village_food_samples_3: So, will you buy my vegetables from now on?
strings.10_village_food_samples_5: You know, being back in business feels good.
strings.10_village_food_samples_6: We might even rack up a surplus and start trading.
strings.10_village_food_samples_7: I have some spare seeds too.
strings.10_village_food_samples_8: If you keep trading with me, that will definitely increase your reputation in the village.
strings.10_village_food_samples_9: And we'll be able to expand my business.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_1: Then maybe you should go find it yourself?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_10: The sewer is gigantic... we'll need more clues to find the place...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_11: Where did this cheese come from?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_13: Hey, it's from Mauritzio's cheese factory... Rivers surround it on three sides.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_14: It used to be the best aged cheese in town.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_15: Yeah, good cheese... a gift from the gods... ha ha.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_16: If only we could reach his cellar where he kept it...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_17: Wait a minute! Maybe the Ancient God is there...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_18: The Old God? Anyway, if you help my guys get into the cellars...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_19: Then half the cheese is yours... and the Ancient God too, of course... ha ha.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_20: Let's go, guys. Drinks on me!
strings.110_town_cheese_find_21: Is that the god who can cure my sister?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_22: I think so... are you starting to believe?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_23: Cheese just appearing out of nowhere... cough-cough
strings.110_town_cheese_find_24: Yes... perhaps... and it might well be my last chance... my cough is growing worse...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_26: Promise me... if I'm gone, will you ask him about Aleksta?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_29: Maybe there's something we can do for your health?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_3: Hey! Don't talk to the customers that way!
strings.110_town_cheese_find_30: There may be a way... but I'm to busy to research it.
strings.110_town_cheese_find_31: Uh... you mind if I take this cheese, by the way?
strings.110_town_cheese_find_6: Tell him... that the price is ridiculous...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_8: I need to find a place in the sewer...
strings.110_town_cheese_find_9: A cell, but not for humans...
strings.110_town_cheese_look_2: You know where Davy the Dagger is?
strings.110_town_cheese_look_3: He's near the sewer entrance, by the west gate...
strings.111_base_dig_1: Ding dong. Bing bang bong. Dig I am! Or am I?
strings.111_base_dig_12: Anyway, I've come here to see you, Keeper Two.
strings.111_base_dig_13: Right now you're the one shaping this story... and shaping the whole world with it.
strings.111_base_dig_14: So I brought you a little gift. Something that lets you see what isn't there.
strings.111_base_dig_15: Your destiny is to take this Red Eye — a fragment of an ancient god's power.
strings.111_base_dig_16: An ancient god... seeing what isn't there... hmm.
strings.111_base_dig_17: Could it help me find a door in a solid wall?
strings.111_base_dig_18: A door? Possibly. But tools like this require... imagination.
strings.111_base_dig_19: Right... because I need that door to free an ancient god. I'd like to talk to him.
strings.111_base_dig_2: What? Who the sard are you?
strings.111_base_dig_20: If I were you... I wouldn't.
strings.111_base_dig_22: Why shouldn't I talk to him?
strings.111_base_dig_23: He seems caring. A good guy, your buddy the ancient god.
strings.111_base_dig_24: He treats the world like it's a play written purely for his own entertainment.
strings.111_base_dig_25: Sometimes he helps the actors. Sometimes he replaces them.
strings.111_base_dig_26: Sometimes he just enjoys watching them suffer. He's dangerous.
strings.111_base_dig_27: How do you know so much about him?
strings.111_base_dig_28: He was the god's High Priest and prophet... am I right?
strings.111_base_dig_3: Nice to meet you, Keeper Two.
strings.111_base_dig_30: Also... there were some golden apples once. Apples that grant absolute wisdom.
strings.111_base_dig_31: Long story short... I ate two of them.
strings.111_base_dig_33: Hmm... how did you get this Red Eye from the god?
strings.111_base_dig_34: Ha... I was just in the right place at the right time. Picked it up off the floor, literally.
strings.111_base_dig_35: Your wife... the Keeper's wife... wished for it with the portal.
strings.111_base_dig_36: But she had no use for it. She wasn't the right type. She wasn't a Keeper.
strings.111_base_dig_37: You, however... You could reshape the world with it.
strings.111_base_dig_38: So I can skip restoring the portal to save the world?
strings.111_base_dig_39: The portal is the core mechanic... I mean... the central power of this world.
strings.111_base_dig_4: How did you get in here? I locked the door.
strings.111_base_dig_40: But I had a feeling you'd need the eye to keep the story moving.
strings.111_base_dig_42: If you really do have endless wisdom, I have a lot of questions.
strings.111_base_dig_43: Too many answers bring too much pain. I've been there.
strings.111_base_dig_44: Besides, I need to catch a ship and leave Town.
strings.111_base_dig_45: When this story ends, I want to be very far away.
strings.111_base_dig_46: Alright then... give me the eye.
strings.111_base_dig_47: How am I supposed to use it?
strings.111_base_dig_48: I thought that guy must have lost his mind after eating those apples.
strings.111_base_dig_49: So... how exactly do you know him, my friend?
strings.111_base_dig_5: Someone must've left it open. These things happen.
strings.111_base_dig_50: Don't start... that's a totally different story from a very long time ago.
strings.111_base_dig_51: Believe me, you wouldn't enjoy hearing it. It would take forever.
strings.111_base_dig_52: Besides, you can probably read about it in some dusty library.
strings.111_base_dig_53: Alright then... If I want any answers, I guess I'll have to go to the sewers and find that door.
strings.111_base_dig_6: Donkey said he saw someone heading this way...
strings.111_base_dig_7: Well hello, Lucius. You've lost some weight I see. Ha ha.
strings.111_base_dig_8: Digus... good to see you! Though I go by Larry now.
strings.111_base_dig_9: Hold on. You two know each other?
strings.112_linda_wealth_2: I did as you asked. The shops are packed with lavish, unnecessary items.
strings.112_linda_wealth_3: I've already seen a surge of wealthy patrons at the club.
strings.112_linda_wealth_4: Well done. You're a hero... to me and to the town. Ha ha...
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_a_1: Now we just have to cure Albert's cough.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_a_2: I can't have him frightening away my best customers!
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_1: After we cure him... with my gentle touch, he can become a very respectable doctor.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_10: I was frozen with fear... Aleksta was the one who saved us.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_11: That day I swore I'd become beautiful and brave.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_13: But it didn't bring me happiness.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_14: Only after meeting Albert have I come to understand. I could truly be happy with him.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_17: I want to thank you... for everything you've done.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_18: I'll be so happy to be near him...
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_19: Is there anything else I can do for you?
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_2: It's the least I can do for him.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_20: You've done enough. I'll speak to Albert myself.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_3: I don't think you owe Albert anything.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_4: Well... yes and no. I was friends with Aleksta. She was so beautiful.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_5: Everyone adored her. I was just the awkward little duckling.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_6: Ha... it's hard to believe that now.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_7: Now I know how to carry myself... how to be admired...
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_8: But back then, I was just jealous.
strings.112_linda_wealth_5_b_9: We were together when the zombies came.
strings.113_sewers_god_1: At last... I was starting to worry it would take you forever.
strings.113_sewers_god_11: Yes. They captured the entire Town. We only recently starting pushing them back.
strings.113_sewers_god_12: Wow... that Keeper sounds like a disaster.
strings.113_sewers_god_13: Did he and his beloved still have the portal?
strings.113_sewers_god_14: No. It was split into fragments. I'm trying to collect them all.
strings.113_sewers_god_15: Hmm... Breaking the portal might be a really bad idea.
strings.113_sewers_god_16: I need you to tell me how to use the portal properly, so I can wish the world back to normal.
strings.113_sewers_god_17: My sister is always being so dramatic. Every couple of years, someone "ruins the world"...
strings.113_sewers_god_18: Yet here we all are, still standing.
strings.113_sewers_god_19: On the other hand, starting fresh somewhere else wouldn't be so bad...
strings.113_sewers_god_2: I was even a little worried I'd run out of cheese to guide you.
strings.113_sewers_god_20: I don't like what I'm hearing. I'll give you your eye back, but only if you help me.
strings.113_sewers_god_21: Ah, these Keepers and their free will...
strings.113_sewers_god_23: I need to know how to use the portal and make the right wish.
strings.113_sewers_god_24: Well, obviously you need the complete portal... all seven stones.
strings.113_sewers_god_25: To activate it, the seven passions... or sins... must stand near it.
strings.113_sewers_god_26: I thought I only needed to collect the fragments. Where do I find the people?
strings.113_sewers_god_27: I wouldn't want to brag, but in my prime, I could activate the portal all by myself.
strings.113_sewers_god_28: So you could activate it for me?
strings.113_sewers_god_29: Not anymore. Being a god sounds impressive, but it drains your passion.
strings.113_sewers_god_3: To be honest, the cheese didn't guide me much... it was mostly just frustrating.
strings.113_sewers_god_30: Then maybe I could do it myself...
strings.113_sewers_god_31: No. I deliberately choose Keepers without all seven passions. No offense.
strings.113_sewers_god_32: None taken. Then how do I activate the portal?
strings.113_sewers_god_33: You must find seven people, one for each day of the week.
strings.113_sewers_god_34: But there's only six days here.
strings.113_sewers_god_35: Yes, I know... six looks better on the wheel of time.
strings.113_sewers_god_37: And how do I find them?
strings.113_sewers_god_38: You probably already have. Or they found you. You'll feel they're special somehow.
strings.113_sewers_god_39: Your connection with them will become clearer.
strings.113_sewers_god_4: You're right... but with such little power left, the cheese hints were the best I could manage.
strings.113_sewers_god_40: Earn their full trust... one hundred percent of it.... and bring them to the portal.
strings.113_sewers_god_42: Yes, that's it. Now my eye, please. I am a god after all.
strings.113_sewers_god_43: With my eye, the portal can work even if you gain only ninety percent of their trust. This will save you some time.
strings.113_sewers_god_5: Anyway... I feel that you have my eye. Give it back now, so you can finish this story.
strings.113_sewers_god_6: I'll regain my power, and you can remain a Keeper for another... let me see... forty years!
strings.113_sewers_god_7: Wait a minute... I think it's my destiny to save the world.
strings.113_sewers_god_9: The fairy, and your sister. They said the other me, Keeper One, ruined the world and awakened the zombie hordes. And the world might die soon.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_1_2: Oh really? One of those Keepers who wants to know everything...
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_1_3: Or we could just skip that part, and go straight to saving the world.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_2_2: I'll gladly answer them after you return my eye.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_1: How did you become a god?
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_2: That happened many years ago... When I was young. Younger than you, actually.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_3: I loved reading history and fantasy books.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_4: I was a dreamer... and through those dreams, and a bit of bad luck, my sister and I ended up here.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_5: There was nothing here but a portal in the void.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_6: It seemed ready to grant our wishes. So I created this world.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_1_7: I never asked to become a god... but I suppose this is how you become one.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_2_2: There's not much I can tell. It was already here when I arrived.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_2_4: Though it tends to twist them in rather awkward ways.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_3_2: She is... or was... a wonderful girl. She loved nature and animals.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_3_3: While I was building my little empire, she spent her time with the trees and the rabbits.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_3_4: I met her. She seems a bit lost now.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_3_5: Truth is, there's not much excitement in simply observing nature.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_3_6: After losing oneself in it for so many years... of course one can become a little strange.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_2: At some point I grew bored with this place.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_3: I decided to travel to other worlds for a while, just to see what things were like elsewhere.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_4: So I came up with a clever plot twist.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_5: The idea was, I'd leave someone from the real world here in my place.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_6: Someone with free will, to keep things running.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_7: A new god... a Keeper. You were all just meant to be my temporary replacements.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_8: But somehow, all of you managed to disappoint me. Too much free will.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_4_9: Not you though. You're a decent Keeper.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_5_2: Oh, all the usual divine powers... lightning bolts, thunder, dramatic entrances... ha ha.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_5_3: Just kidding. My real power is my imagination.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_5_5: And my eye helps me see interesting ways to bring those things to life.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_5_6: I used to believe in my own power...
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_5_7: But now I rely on other people's faith in me.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_1: Why do you need the red eye?
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_2: I told you... It helps me. It reveals what is hidden.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_3: It brings ideas to the surface.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_4: But it also gives you magical power, right?
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_5: Not exactly... it's more like a curse.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_6_6: But I found a way to control it... and even enjoy it.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_7_1: How did you lose your eye?
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_7_2: Someone not very bright decided to punish me, using the power of the portal.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_7_3: But instead he only cursed himself.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_7_4: Though to be honest, being locked up with all that cheese was not very pleasant.
strings.113_sewers_god_ask_3_7_5: So I suppose I was punished after all.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_2: Alright. A deal is a deal. Here's your eye. But I still need your help.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_3: Of course. I'm a good god, after all... though I have but little power left.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_4: I require some faith. Please perform my ritual.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_5: That wasn't part of the deal.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_6: It will be much faster than earning that last ten percent of trust.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_7: So... complete the portal, gain the trust of six people, and perform the ritual.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_8: In any order... but I suggest you hurry with the ritual. Then I can help you with those six.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_9: Farewell... I have some godly business to attend to.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_after_2: I have things to do, and you must perform a ceremony for me.
strings.113_sewers_god_give_eye_after_3: Let's focus on that. I'll answer your questions afterward. I promise.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_10: I could repair the attic in my house. Would that suit you?
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_11: Ha ha... a fine place for a powerless god.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_12: Let me know when it's ready.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_2: That's quite a lot to process.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_3: While I'm fixing the portal and thinking all this through, I'd better hold on to the eye.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_4: Oh Keeper, don't make me regret this.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_5: You'll get it back once I save the world.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_6: A poor decision indeed... but I suppose free will is free will.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_7: Still, I cannot remain here any longer, surrounded by mountains of cheese.
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_8: I'm not really sure where you could stay...
strings.113_sewers_god_keep_eye_9: Well, I could stay at your place for a while.
strings.114_base_god_1: Impressive... just like in the old days. They built this temple to earn my forgiveness.
strings.114_base_god_10: And I am. I'm quietly removing their last doubts. But the final step is yours.
strings.114_base_god_13: You know, I once knew a man who went mad from having too many answers.
strings.114_base_god_14: I like you, and I don't want to see you go mad... So you can ask two questions.
strings.114_base_god_2: But they forgot — not everything is about walls.
strings.114_base_god_4: Yes. I regained it even before the ceremony. Your own belief in me was enough.
strings.114_base_god_5: Still... I must admit, the ceremony was rather pleasant.
strings.114_base_god_6: I'm glad you liked it. Now tell me more about those six people.
strings.114_base_god_7: Simple. Just go to them, and ask for their help activating the magic portal.
strings.114_base_god_8: You might offer them a wish from the portal as payment. That usually works.
strings.114_base_god_9: You said you'd help me convince them.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_1: Hey Albert. It's nice to see you moved into a proper house.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_10: He's doing a lot... even helping me run the Club.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_11: Linda deserves some help. A beautiful girl like her shouldn't have to work all day.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_13: I'm glad you two met. Maybe there's something I can do for you.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_14: Actually, yes. I've run out of bottles for my medicine.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_15: The demand is enormous these days. Could you craft some for me? Something... appropriately professional.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_16: Oh, poor girl... let me help.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_18: Oh, I think she's doing fine.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_19: Alright, I need to get back to my patients. I'll see you later with the bottles.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_2: Yes... Linda can be very persuasive.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_22: I heard you asking how you could help us.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_24: Could you bring me some chocolate? I heard it's quite special.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_25: The merchants recently brought some cocoa seeds.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_26: Sure, I'll see what I can do.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_3: If only. He built a laboratory in the basement, and spends all his time down there.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_4: But I also opened a small office on the second floor for patients.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_5: I'm only teasing. I can see you're really trying to change... and I respect that.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_6: Hold on... Albert, is that your sister working behind the bar?
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_7: Yes, that's Aleksta. We taught her how to serve beer.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_8: Linda and I thought it might help with her recovery.
strings.115_linda_dawn_ask_9: But I'm still doing my experiments. Of course between Linda and all the clients, I don't have as much time.
strings.116_base_attic_1: Behold! I sensed my new residence was ready, so I arrived.
strings.116_base_attic_10: No, I don't. Now that you have a place to stay, tell me more about those six people.
strings.116_base_attic_11: You just need to ask them for a favor... to help you activate the magic portal.
strings.116_base_attic_12: You can bribe them with promises of portal wishes.
strings.116_base_attic_13: That sounds like a decent plan.
strings.116_base_attic_14: Exactly. Repair the portal, convince the six... and don't forget to invite me!
strings.116_base_attic_15: After all, you'll still need me to perform a small trick before you can make proper wishes.
strings.116_base_attic_16: Naturally... you wouldn't want us doing it all without you.
strings.116_base_attic_18: Can you tell me who those six are?
strings.116_base_attic_19: You really don't know? I thought you were an experienced Keeper.
strings.116_base_attic_2: Psst... I saw him hiding in a nearby bush for quite some time.
strings.116_base_attic_20: I just want to be sure.
strings.116_base_attic_21: Yes, yes... better safe than sorry. Six sins ... six people.
strings.116_base_attic_22: Linda, the owner of the Dockside Club. Albert the doctor.
strings.116_base_attic_23: Agatha the nun. Herbert the guard.
strings.116_base_attic_24: Gunter the... PR manager. And Jack the craftsman.
strings.116_base_attic_25: But there are seven stones... who activates the last one?
strings.116_base_attic_26: As far as I know, that always happens rather mysteriously. Someone appears at the last moment.
strings.116_base_attic_27: I suppose it's meant to teach a valuable lesson.
strings.116_base_attic_28: Well... you are a god after all.
strings.116_base_attic_29: Yes, a god living in your attic.
strings.116_base_attic_3: Follow me, I'll show you to your attic.
strings.116_base_attic_30: So, how's our ancient god doing?
strings.116_base_attic_31: You know... he actually seems like a reasonably nice guy.
strings.116_base_attic_32: Still, it's strange having a god living in your attic.
strings.116_base_attic_33: A talking skull is strange too, but I got used to it.
strings.116_base_attic_34: What bothers me is the red eye. I don't feel comfortable having it.
strings.116_base_attic_35: Then give it back... or give it to me, ha ha.
strings.116_base_attic_36: Anyway, right now I need to talk to the people who can help me activate the portal.
strings.116_base_attic_37: Good luck with that. It's not something you ask every day.
strings.116_base_attic_38: Exactly... they'll need to trust me completely. I'll need to pick the right moment to ask.
strings.116_base_attic_5: It's quite a lovely place here for you to stay.
strings.116_base_attic_6: Yes... to be honest, I haven't had a home for a long time.
strings.116_base_attic_7: And this place reminds me of my summer vacations when I was a child.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_1: Hello. Hope I'm not disturbing you.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_10: Honestly... I'm not sure we need anything else.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_11: I see you're almost done with the book I gave you.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_12: I could bring you more if you like.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_13: That would be nice, wouldn't it, Agatha?
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_15: You might enjoy this one, Herbert... but I can't read any more of that dreck.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_16: You know, I'm something of a writer myself. I could try writing a book for you.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_17: A trilogy, maybe. I heard all good stories come in threes.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_19: Good thing you know how to write, Keeper.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_20: Herbert tells me so many stories about his military past.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_21: If I only knew how to write them down.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_22: Wait a minute... I thought you knew how to read.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_23: Reading, yes... not writing. Nuns are meant to read the holy words, not write new ones.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_24: Hmm... I've been thinking about the design for a semi-automatic device that can write down speech.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_25: I'll bring you one to try.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_26: My old war stories are nothing special.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_27: But I like them... and I want to hold on to them.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_28: Then I'm glad we found a way I can help.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_3: You built a wonderful place for Agatha and me.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_4: And the best part... it's not far from my work. Ha ha.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_5: Ha ha... That was a good one, Agatha.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_6: That must be the first joke I ever heard from her.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_7: Looks like you two finally found some peace.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_8: Strange as it sounds... I haven't felt any anger for quite a while.
strings.117_crossroad_calm_ask_9: That makes me happy. Maybe there's something I could do to make life even more peaceful for you?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_10: It's all about the process, and working together with your friends.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_11: Even small achievements feel better when you reach them together.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_12: Hey, I'm your friend too. Maybe I could join the project?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_13: Well... we're trying to keep things small and avoid bureaucracy.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_14: Alright, fair enough. But maybe I could help as an outsourcer?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_15: Hmm... I think we already have everything covered. Right, Jack?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_17: Still, I remember you talking about a second prosthetic hand.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_18: Which would let you work twice as fast.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_19: And Gunter, I could build you a small printing press. You could publish your poems and updates about the colossus.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_2: As you can see, we already started that project I told you about.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_20: That might help, don't you think?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_21: Do you really think people will want to read my poetry and the colossus reports?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_22: Of course they will. You're a brilliant poet.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_23: Well... in that case, we'll gladly accept the help.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_3: No way... you're actually planning to rebuild the colossus?
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_4: Exactly! I even made a public announcement. Everyone's excited.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_5: There's some people from overseas who want to come see the progress.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_6: What was that word you used, Gunter... tu...
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_7: Tourism! Rebuilding the colossus will attract visitors.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_8: We're even planning a tour with Davy to the infected part of Town.
strings.118_astrologer_project_ask_9: Big plans, guys! But don't you think this project might be too big for the two of you?
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_2: Like we talked about before, I have a clear target.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_3: Tell me, and I'll try to convince you not to do it.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_4: This time it's important. I need to drain the water from the lock.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_5: Then you'll have to close the left gate of the lock.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_6: Lucky for you, it's not far from our defensive position at the Market Square.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_7: Though my guards are reporting there's more zombies gathering on the far side of the bridge.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_8: I still need to do it, Herbert.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_herbert_9: Alright. You're a reasonable man, after all. I'll inform my guards about the coming battle.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_10: Then wait for the right moment, and make a quick push to the gate.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_2: Hi lads... It seems I need to cross the bridge with my troops.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_3: Long time no see. I thought we were done attacking.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_4: I hope we don't move our barricade any farther.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_5: Ha! I agree. Having the market this close is quite comfortable.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_6: We'll keep this as our main defensive position.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_7: We only need a quick attack, so I can close the ship lock gate.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_pre_9: Hmm... you'll need a solid defense to hold the square across the bridge.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_1: Sard... these gates are heavier than I thought.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_10: Good lads. And now I need to talk with your commander.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_2: I don't have time to bring my zombies in to help.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_3: Told you he'd need our help!
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_4: What are you doing here, lads?!
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_5: We're here to help you close the gates! Or are you managing fine on your own?
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_7: I'll be bragging for a month that I helped the Keeper.
strings.119_pre-B1-fights_win_9: Yes, we shouldn't leave our post for too long.
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_10: And everybody's just... kinda okay with it.
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_14: So with a little faith on your side, you'll fight the zombies back?
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_15: Maybe... We can try it at least.
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_16: But I can't imagine where you're going to find enough faith...
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_3: "You don't have to shout good news. It need only be whispered."
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_4: I can't help but ask, what's with the quotes?
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_5: Oh, never mind. It's just from a book I like.
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_6: So what's your plan? Are we going to gather some supplies and fight the zombies back?
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_8: All we've been doing is retreating... and losing faith.
strings.11_guards_morale_graveyard_9: Seems there's nowhere left to retreat... and no faith left to lose.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_1: At last! Is that the Royal Foundry?
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_2: It is indeed... though we weren't expecting any visitors. Where did you come from?
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_3: The path to the safe part of Town is clear now.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_4: Oh thank God... we were praying that others survived.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_5: Yes, the Town is still pretty functional.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_6: That's wonderful news. Maybe now we can finally eat something other than fish from the water tunnel.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_7: Of course... but first I need to speak with the bishop.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_foundry_8: He's not a bishop anymore. He's our brother now. He's over there.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_herbert_2: I have a new target. It's the entrance to the water tunnel on the right side of the ship lock.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_herbert_3: Ah yes, I know that tunnel.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_herbert_4: Good thing you drained the lock... the passage should be dry now.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_herbert_6: Definitely not from the square. Instead, attack from the bridge on the port side.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_herbert_7: From there, the road to the tunnel entrance is almost a straight shot.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_10: He never mentioned it connected to the sewers.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_2: Hello lads... looks like I need to reach the water tunnel from here.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_3: It's not far, but the road ahead is crawling with zombies.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_4: Keep your eyes open, too. They might jump out from the houses along the street.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_5: Thanks, lads. The mission seems pretty straightforward.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_7: I thought that tunnel connected to the sewers. Doesn't it?
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_8: Don't look at me. I've got no idea.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_pre_9: Well, I spoke with a master who knows everything about the tunnels.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_1: This should be the entrance to the tunnel...
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_10: New orders are available... ha ha.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_11: What about the water tunnel to the royal foundry?
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_12: Oh, that place? Completely overrun with undead.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_13: I need to reach that foundry.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_14: And you came here from the surface? You're a legend, my friend!
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_15: But next time, just use the sewer.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_16: Yes... next time I'll use the sewer.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_18: Hey guys, I need to get to the water tunnel leading to the foundry.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_19: Easy... left, right, left, left, left, right...
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_2: Sard... this tunnel is full of rats!
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_20: No, not left, right... left, left.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_21: Guys... Maybe you could just show me the way?
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_4: Well, well... what a pleasant surprise. Good day, Keeper.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_6: Through the sewer, of course. Once the lock drained, new routes opened up.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_7: I thought you avoided going underground yourself.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_8: Normally I do. But this is a special opportunity.
strings.120_pre-B2-fights_win_9: The wealthy district is now within reach... new business opportunities, you see.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_2: Now that the lock is empty, we need to secure the bottom.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_3: What's the point? It's just a bunch of dirt.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_4: It may be dirt to you, but I know some people who call it soil.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_5: And I promised it to them.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_6: A man's word is the most valuable thing he has.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_7: You'll need to push through from Market Square. Clear the path, and barricade the area afterward.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_herbert_8: Understood. I'll take care of it.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_2: Hello lads... looks like I'll be crossing the bridge again.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_3: This time I'm reclaiming the bottom of the lock.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_4: What do you need that for?
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_5: He's obviously planning something. After all those years, the soil down there must be excellent.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_6: You're absolutely right, my friend. Do you have any advice?
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_7: Make sure you barricade the place once you secure it.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_pre_8: That shouldn't be hard. There's plenty of debris down there.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_1: Alright, the place is safe now. I just need to check the barricade.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_2: The barricade seems solid. This place is safe now.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_3: Wait a minute... how am I supposed to get out of here?
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_4: Here, guys. Let's find the driest place first.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_6: Through the sewers. We wanted to settle before you changed your mind.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_7: As soon as we heard where you were headed, we followed.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_8: In case you took it for yourself.
strings.121_pre-B3-fights_win_9: Bless the soul who invented the sewer system.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_10: Yes, just make sure you hold the bank before crossing.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_11: Thanks, lads. Your advice never disappoints.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_2: This time, lads, I need to reach the people living on the western lake.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_3: The carpenters? They're probably safe in those houses on stilts.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_4: You don't even need to fight. Just take a boat.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_5: Do you see any boats here?
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_6: Then I better just fight my way through. After all, I have an army for a reason.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_8: Just move across the square and secure the bank.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_pre_9: Once you reach the wooden bridges, the rest should be easy.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_1: Hey you over there! Lower the bridge!
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_10: Maybe because I don't have one.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_11: Good thing we do. You can use it on your way back.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_12: Thanks... I'd also like to get some excellent wood from you.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_13: Then you'll need to talk with our master.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_3: Do you even know who that is?
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_5: I'm a Keeper... the Graveyard Keeper.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_6: I don't know him, but he sure sounds confident.
strings.122_pre-B5-fights_win_9: Why didn't you just take a boat?
strings.123_basement_factory_elevator_1: Wow... how interesting. What can it be?
strings.123_basement_factory_elevator_2: Drawing from my Graveyard Keeper knowledge, it’s some kind of elevator for resources.
strings.123_basement_factory_elevator_3: If I can restore it, I'll be able to move items from here to the surface.
strings.123_basement_factory_factory_1: I told you clearing that debris would be worth it.
strings.123_basement_factory_factory_2: I have to agree... It’ll take a lot of work to restore everything... but the potential is very promising.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_1: Hey, you started without me again!
strings.123_basement_factory_find_10: I don’t know what that means, but I bet you can...
strings.123_basement_factory_find_11: And here you can rebuild the part that puts the whole thing in motion.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_12: You just need some poor fellows to turn it.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_13: Where would I find someone willing to turn it down here underground?
strings.123_basement_factory_find_14: Well, for example... maybe you can use some of those undead fellows wandering around our yard.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_2: Relax, I’d call you if I found anything interesting.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_3: That’s exactly the problem... you wouldn’t recognize something interesting.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_4: Seems like there’s nothing interesting here...
strings.123_basement_factory_find_5: See, that’s exactly what I’m talking about.
strings.123_basement_factory_find_7: Look, it all connects with gears under the ground...
strings.123_basement_factory_find_8: I bet you can place something that moves over there...
strings.123_basement_factory_mine_2: I don’t know, but it seems like it should be a path to the forest.
strings.123_basement_factory_mine_3: I bet this is the path to the forest mine!
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_1: Do you hear that sound behind this debris? Some kind of clinking.
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_2: That echo... there’s a space behind this. A big space.
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_3: This debris looks like it will be hard to clear... and after that I’ll need to reinforce the ceiling.
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_4: I'm not sure it’s worth the trouble.
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_5: But there's got to be something valuable over there!
strings.123_basement_factory_pass_6: Metal, gears... sounds like a machine graveyard.
strings.124_village_money_chest_2: Here, guys... I crafted some money for you.
strings.124_village_money_chest_5: You’re right! Ok, here's the chest like we agreed.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_10: And then I can stamp them with the royal seal.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_12: But if we want a full budget, we’ll need a lot of them.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_13: I’ll fire up my printing machine as soon as I can.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_2: I just had a rather awkward conversation with Jeffry and Heffry.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_3: They asked me to craft some money for the town budget.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_4: Heh... they’re so naive. But we actually do have a problem.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_5: The economy is growing, and we’re running out of coins.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_6: If only we could actually craft money... I don’t know — maybe out of paper! Ha ha.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_7: Hmm... you know, that could actually work.
strings.124_village_money_januarius_8: No, I was just kidding. Who would buy paper money?
strings.124_village_money_januarius_9: I’ll try to make colorful paper bank notes.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_10: You're a wise tavern keeper, my friend!
strings.124_village_money_stamp_12: I’m honestly surprised... just imagine the possibilities this opens...
strings.124_village_money_stamp_2: I made some... and they look surprisingly good. We just need a royal stamp to make them official.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_3: That's convenient... I just happen to have one. It came with the election guide.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_4: I think it's only fair for you to take your cut.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_5: I just hope people will buy it.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_6: Oh, they will. I’m almost sure of it.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_7: And then I’ll make some more.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_8: I have a feeling we should be careful.
strings.124_village_money_stamp_9: Let’s wait until the town grows a bit first, and only print more after that.
strings.124_village_money_twins_10: I don’t think you understand how this works.
strings.124_village_money_twins_11: We’ll give you this mystery chest we pulled out of the river.
strings.124_village_money_twins_12: Yeah... We couldn’t open it anyway.
strings.124_village_money_twins_13: Hmm... a mystery chest does sound tempting.
strings.124_village_money_twins_4: What’s the difference? Januarius won’t let us spend any money.
strings.124_village_money_twins_5: What money are you talking about?
strings.124_village_money_twins_6: The budget... you know, the money we’re supposed to spend.
strings.124_village_money_twins_7: Yeah... but it’s empty. He said first we need to make some money.
strings.124_village_money_twins_8: But we don’t even know what money is made of.
strings.124_village_money_twins_9: Hey, Keeper... you make things all the time. Can you go to Januarius and craft some money for us?
strings.125_astrologer_third_10: Fine. Come back on <sprite name="day_lust"> with the money, and it's yours.
strings.125_astrologer_third_11: I don't know how to spell such a big number, so I'll write it down for you.
strings.125_astrologer_third_13: Half the original price, plus my commission.
strings.125_astrologer_third_3: I'm trying to buy back an ancient fragment of the magic portal.
strings.125_astrologer_third_4: Gunter sold it to a merchant.
strings.125_astrologer_third_5: Oh yes, he certainly did... and I collected my fee.
strings.125_astrologer_third_6: He's quite the showman... "Mystical relic! Ancient power!"
strings.125_astrologer_third_7: The merchant keeps bringing it up every week...
strings.125_astrologer_third_8: He hasn't managed to sell it. Not even for half price.
strings.125_astrologer_third_9: Perfect. I'll take it off his hands.
strings.125_astrologer_third_buy_3: And here's your stone... Quite a "magical" one. Ha ha.
strings.125_astrologer_third_buy_4: Great... I should put this one in place and find out where the next one is.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_10: Yikes... it's deep in the mud... I don't know the word...
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_11: A small channel with gates that let ships pass.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_13: I already drained it. It should be easy to retrieve.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_14: Hey... maybe we should ask the mirror about the next one?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_16: Mirror... mirror... show us the fifth portal fragment.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_17: Well... this is awkward. How many fragments did you actually have?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_2: I always felt so guilty about selling it.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_20: The others went traveling, and left their fragments with me.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_21: And I recently gave the fifth one to my friend... Jack.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_22: Why would Jack need a portal fragment?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_23: Don't shout... I just... He's been pretty miserable lately, haven't you noticed?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_24: So you gave him an ancient magical relic for emotional support?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_25: It seemed reasonable at the time.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_26: In any case, we should probably address his mood.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_29: You remember how he used to be... full of energy, so self-confident.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_3: It's part of our history... Imagine it ending up in some island museum.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_30: Now I see doubt in his eyes.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_31: His factory project isn't really going the way he planned.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_32: I know. As his friend, I should get him into something new.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_33: Something meaningful and visible to the townspeople.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_34: He's still the town's hero, after all.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_36: I'm a man of my word...
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_37: Our PR campaign has to hit its targets before I can shift focus.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_39: A respectable number of likes <sprite name="happiness"> in the weekly report.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_40: I think that's mostly my responsibility. You can move on with Jack.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_41: I need the numbers... not only as a PR manager, but also as an astrologer.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_42: Ah... the stars disapprove of low engagement.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_5: I have one question... how did you manage to spend so much money?
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_6: Ah... I never mentioned? Before astrology, I was a professional investor.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_7: So if you're ever looking for opportunities...
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_8: Right. Let's find the fourth fragment.
strings.125_astrologer_third_install_9: Mirror... mirror... reveal the fourth portal piece.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_1: Hey, what do you think you're doing?
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_10: Apparently there's a trick to making wishes. Our ancient god is keeping that detail to himself.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_11: But he promised to reveal it when the portal is ready.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_12: Alright then... time to meet our more beautiful twins. Ha ha.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_2: Leaving your old friend Larry behind?
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_3: I'm not sure the coming battle is the safest place for you.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_4: Relax. I'll ride in your bag like in the old days. I barely weigh anything.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_5: Besides, I want to meet that other talking skull... the one that supposedly looks better.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_6: You're right, Larry. We started this story together, we should finish it together.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_7: Have you thought about your wish yet?
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_8: I'll probably wish to save the world... whatever that means.
strings.126_pre-C1-fights_9: That's the spirit. I'm proud of you.
strings.127_palace_battle_10: I told you I'd be watching.
strings.127_palace_battle_12: How nice that a god is on our side.
strings.127_palace_battle_13: Good thing I kept the red eye. I know how to reveal hidden doors with it.
strings.127_palace_battle_14: Honestly, why bother with a god, when your friend can do all the same tricks?
strings.127_palace_battle_16: Don't worry, pal. We've got all the time in the world. We can try again another day.
strings.127_palace_battle_2: I think we can hold this position. That should give us enough time to reach the Palace.
strings.127_palace_battle_4: The path goes uphill from here. The secret door should be somewhere along the way.
strings.127_palace_battle_5: And where exactly is that door?
strings.127_palace_battle_6: I don't know. It's marked here on the map.
strings.127_palace_battle_7: Or maybe Davy tricked you. Sounds like his style.
strings.127_palace_battle_8: I don't know, Larry... this might be a disaster. Maybe all of this was for nothing.
strings.128_foundry_wine_give_2: Just don’t drink too much or too fast, okay?
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_1: I noticed that you’re looking at me like you want to ask something.
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_10: And we would very much like to be closer to God.
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_11: There’s some logic in that... but you’ll need excellent wine for such a task.
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_12: Probably so... We don’t have money, but we can offer you this sword instead.
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_2: Yes, good Keeper... you’re from the Town, right?
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_4: We’ve never been there... do they have wine in your Town?
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_5: Oh yes... probably more than we need.
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_7: Are you even allowed to drink alcohol?
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_8: We’re not sure... the Bishop... I mean Brother Bishop...
strings.128_foundry_wine_monk_9: He said good wine brings you closer to God.
strings.129_palace_keeper_1: One trip through the empty palace later...
strings.129_palace_keeper_10: I just wanted to go home...
strings.129_palace_keeper_11: We both wanted to go home. But instead we got stuck in this nightmare.
strings.129_palace_keeper_13: I see. But the portal is still our only chance to set everything right... and send you home.
strings.129_palace_keeper_14: The problem is, the portal is gone. It was shattered into pieces.
strings.129_palace_keeper_15: Luckily, I have all the pieces but one... and it's somewhere around here.
strings.129_palace_keeper_16: Ha ha... no one expected a second talking skull, did they?
strings.129_palace_keeper_17: Lucius, old friend... is that you?
strings.129_palace_keeper_18: Who else, Jove? After all, we share the same curse.
strings.129_palace_keeper_19: This is all very touching, but maybe we should talk somewhere safer.
strings.129_palace_keeper_20: I don't think my army can hold off all those zombies for much longer.
strings.129_palace_keeper_21: I can buy us some time. I've never tried ringing this in the middle of the day before...
strings.129_palace_keeper_22: But it probably won't make things worse.
strings.129_palace_keeper_24: Judging from recent events... things just got worse.
strings.129_palace_keeper_27: I can still hear the sounds of battle... that's a good sign.
strings.129_palace_keeper_3: Not when you're wearing full plate armor.
strings.129_palace_keeper_30: Wait a moment... I need to catch my breath.
strings.129_palace_keeper_31: Alright... I think we're safe here for now. We can rest a little.
strings.129_palace_keeper_32: Besides, I have a lot of questions.
strings.129_palace_keeper_33: Yes... I should explain what happened.
strings.129_palace_keeper_34: How much do you already know?
strings.129_palace_keeper_35: I spent the last eight years chained up in a dungeon.
strings.129_palace_keeper_36: Oh. Alright then... I'll start from the beginning.
strings.129_palace_keeper_37: And to be clear... I didn't know if that other part of me is even still alive...
strings.129_palace_keeper_38: I found myself in this world, and a man with a red eye gave me the job of Graveyard Keeper.
strings.129_palace_keeper_39: But my only real goal was to return to my wife.
strings.129_palace_keeper_4: If you're here to punish me, you should know that I'm immortal!
strings.129_palace_keeper_40: Long story short... I learned about a portal that could send me home.
strings.129_palace_keeper_41: Eventually I figured out how to activate it.
strings.129_palace_keeper_42: But instead of sending me home, it brought my love here.
strings.129_palace_keeper_43: Apparently, by using the portal, I broke some ancient contract.
strings.129_palace_keeper_44: After that... everything started falling apart.
strings.129_palace_keeper_45: And just so you know... it all happened because of the man with the red eye.
strings.129_palace_keeper_46: So I decided to use the portal one more time, to punish him and take away his power.
strings.129_palace_keeper_47: But instead it corrupted me... and I couldn't stop making new wishes.
strings.129_palace_keeper_48: Instead of going home, I wished for power and wealth.
strings.129_palace_keeper_49: Until our friends destroyed the portal.
strings.129_palace_keeper_5: This was all a huge mistake
strings.129_palace_keeper_50: Then I cursed all of them... the whole Town...
strings.129_palace_keeper_51: In a desperate attempt to restore the portal, I raised an undead army.
strings.129_palace_keeper_52: It's alright, darling... you were possessed.
strings.129_palace_keeper_53: Yes, my dear. Your love saved me... it gave me the strength to get rid of the eye.
strings.129_palace_keeper_54: That's how we became trapped in the Palace... unable to control the evil we unleashed.
strings.129_palace_keeper_55: Although we did still have the bell... to call off the zombies once a week.
strings.129_palace_keeper_56: Yes, they were supposed to find the portal fragments, so we could fix everything.
strings.129_palace_keeper_57: But they always failed... They only brought us useless junk.
strings.129_palace_keeper_58: Well, the food and the booze were good at least.
strings.129_palace_keeper_59: Ha ha... that explains why the zombies retreat at the sound of the bell.
strings.129_palace_keeper_6: If anyone deserves punishment here, it's me...
strings.129_palace_keeper_60: Good thing my zombie army is much better organized than that.
strings.129_palace_keeper_61: Now we're finally close to fixing the portal. Let's move.
strings.129_palace_keeper_62: You know... I still don't understand why they never tried to find you.
strings.129_palace_keeper_63: I think they were happy together... just the two of them.
strings.129_palace_keeper_7: I'm not here to punish anyone...
strings.129_palace_keeper_9: Phew... what a relief. You're the only one who can understand me.
strings.12_village_boat_brothers_2: Are you guys ready to row to the port?
strings.12_village_boat_brothers_3: Hooray, we're about to have a boat again!
strings.12_village_boat_brothers_4: Yeah, I wouldn't be so thrilled. The Shop Foreman's gifts are never free...
strings.12_village_boat_finally_2: Yep, everything is ready. We're just waiting for right wind!
strings.12_village_boat_finally_3: I'll send you a message on our return.
strings.12_village_boat_tools_2: Thanks! Once I get my workshop back, I'll take you on as an apprentice.
strings.12_village_boat_tools_3: Now, ask the brothers if they're ready for the trip to the port.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_11: They told me they'd agree... if someone they trust asked them.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_3: There are some... complications with building the boat.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_4: But don't worry, I'm a professional!
strings.12_village_boat_wood_5: I just need a set bronze tools.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_6: You can't really get them in the village.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_7: Is that all you need? Just so I don't run back and forth.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_8: Don't worry, that's the last thing I need.
strings.12_village_boat_wood_9: ... Oh wait... I also need those two boys in matching outfits there to row.
strings.130_town_wishes_almost_10: Keeper, the barricades are in trouble!
